title: The Electronic Structure of Transition Metal Oxides in Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy
content: Understanding of the electronic structure of materials is crucial to evaluate and tailor their physical properties such as electric and thermal conductivity, magnetic susceptibility, and catalytic activity, among others. Especially important are Transition Metal Compounds which play a critical role in industrial applications such as Lithium-ion batteries, solar cells, steel and superalloys, memory devices and catalysis [1, 2]. For instance, the cuprate superconductors made from CuO2 layers, are considered as the highest temperature superconductors (HTSCs) where the tuning the Cu oxidation state to control the density of charge carries enables real-world applications, including Maglev trains, medical imaging and quantum computing [3, 4]. In ferromagnetic oxides heterostructures such as La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/NdNiO3, the charge transfer between Mn and Ni at the interface is found to be the driving force of the magnetism at the interface [4, 5].
